- response projects_scanned (full 37k name list ~793KB · 95% of payload, pure
  noise — each hit carries its own project) capped to count + 20 sample.

scope=project no regression. Perf root (37k-dir scan) → consolidation main-line.

situation: fix(bridge): decode stdin as UTF-8, not Windows gbk (CJK obs ingest crash) (#37) (2026-06-06)
content:

fix(bridge): decode stdin as UTF-8, not Windows gbk (CJK obs ingest crash) (#37)
Root cause (SSH+repro confirmed): on a Chinese Windows host sys.stdin defaults

(binary) + decode UTF-8 explicitly (errors=replace · crash-proof, never produces
a surrogate). 5 TDD tests (CJK name, punctuation, ascii, invalid bytes).

situation: fix(daemon): P6 · cap BLAS/OMP/torch internal threads to 1 · root-cure CPU thrash (2026-05-22)
content:
commit 66801b7ada6b 2026-05-22
fix(daemon): P6 · cap BLAS/OMP/torch internal threads to 1 · root-cure CPU thrash
P4 (59661ff) bounded the pool to 8 workers.
P5 (1460c10) removed the global lock around embed.

But under sustained V5/V7/Kairos concurrent ingest load, the daemon
still degraded within ~19 minutes:
  - CPU 206% sustained (vs 67% post-restart)
  - 24 CLOSE_WAIT accumulated
  - ingest timeout at 10s, even 30s
  - 46 threads (vs 9 healthy)

Root cause: each BGE encode call spawns 4-8 BLAS/OMP/MKL internal
threads by default. With 8 pool workers each encoding concurrently,
8 × 4 = 32 internal threads thrash on the 4-core CPU. Cache
invalidation + context switches dominate; useful work stalls.

P6 fix (CRITICAL: must be in daemon.py BEFORE any numpy/torch import):
  os.environ.setdefault("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "1")
  os.environ.setdefault("MKL_NUM_THREADS", "1")
  os.environ.setdefault("OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS", "1")
  os.environ.setdefault("NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS", "1")
  torch.set_num_threads(1)
  torch.set_num_interop_threads(1)

Result: 8 workers × 1 internal thread = 8 threads on 4 cores · clean.

Verified post-deploy stress test:
  · 20 concurrent ingest · ALL 20/20 ok in 5.02s wall time
  · mean per-request 3.36s · max 4.92s
  · CLOSE_WAIT: 1 (vs 24 before P6, was 209 before P5)
  · daemo

situation: fix(daemon): P5 · remove global lock around embed · true root cure for CLOSE_WAIT pileup (2026-05-22)
content:
commit 1460c103dd3e 2026-05-22
fix(daemon): P5 · remove global lock around embed · true root cure for CLOSE_WAIT pileup
P4 (commit 59661ff) capped thread count via ThreadPoolExecutor(8) but
the global `_state["lock"]` inside handle_request still serialized
all 8 workers behind one BGE encode call. Under V5/V7/Kairos high-
frequency ingest + recall traffic, this resulted in:

  2026-05-22 production · pid 1477115 · 4h12min uptime
    · CPU 196% sustained (1-2 threads embedding, 8 workers waiting on lock)
    · 209 CLOSE_WAIT sockets (clients timed out at 10s while their
      request was queued behind the lock; daemon thread held FD until
      it eventually acquired and returned)
    · ingest action: 10s timeout (verified via direct probe)

V5 dialog fell back to HTTP path (compass.service v0.9 :8770) which
worked but defeated the latency benefit of BGE-daemon direct socket.

P5 fix:
  Remove `with _state["lock"]:` wrapper around the entire handle_request
  body. BGE-m3 + sentence-transformers + torch internals are thread-safe
  (GIL protects dict ops · torch.no_grad context is reentrant). The
  lock was overly broad; removing it lets 8 workers encode concurrently.

  Dedented the formerly-locked block (recall/drift logic + verification
  log write) by 4 spaces.

Verified post-deploy on cloud:
  · 1

situation: fix(daemon): P4 · bounded thread pool · root-cause fix for recall timeout (2026-05-22)
content:
commit 59661ff5d4db 2026-05-22
fix(daemon): P4 · bounded thread pool · root-cause fix for recall timeout
The BGE daemon was spawning one unbounded `threading.Thread` per
incoming connection (daemon.py:495 prior to this fix). Under V5/V7
retry storms, threads accumulated faster than they finished:
  - Observed 2026-05-22: 288 threads leaked, 254% sustained CPU,
    10h35min CPU consumed in 4h10min wall time
  - 15+ sockets stuck in CLOSE_WAIT (clients timed out and disconnected
    while handler threads were still blocked in `_state[lock]`)
  - Recall requests timed out at 30s+ for projects with only 2 entries
    because the global lock serialized work behind a single slow request

Fix:
  1. Replace `threading.Thread(target=handle_conn, ...).start()` with
     `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8).submit(handle_conn, conn)`.
     Thread count is now bounded · retry storms can't grow it past 8.
  2. Bump `sock.listen()` backlog from 8 → 128 so momentary burst waits
     at the OS level instead of being refused (which retry-stormed
     callers would only amplify).
  3. Pool size configurable via env COMPASS_DAEMON_POOL · default 8 ·
     matches 4-core CPU's effective concurrency for BGE-m3 inference.

Verified on cloud /opt/nautilus-compass-v1/daemon.py after deploy:
  - threads stable a

claude-code dialogs only had tools.read/tools.write — caused this fail.

goes brittle · they cover the full lifecycle Claude Code drives, not

situation: fix(ops): Connection: close on /v1/v14/* · true root-cause fix for V5 RemoteProtocolError (2026-05-12)
content:
commit 74ec8f4d5b65 2026-05-12
fix(ops): Connection: close on /v1/v14/* · true root-cause fix for V5 RemoteProtocolError
Why keep-alive 75 (commit 50708a2) was insufficient:
- V5/V6 production call recall every 10-15 min · idle gap >> 75s
- Previous smoke used 10s idle · false-positive
- V7 retry decorator reused stale pool conn · 2nd attempt also failed

Real fix:
- Middleware adds `Connection: close` header for /v1/v14/* paths only
- httpx honors HTTP/1.1 Connection: close · drops pool entry · next call fresh TCP
- /v1/drift_check unchanged · high-freq · keep-alive pool reuse OK

Verified:
- curl: /v1/v14/recall returns Connection: close ✓
- curl: /v1/drift_check returns no Connection header ✓
- smoke_long_idle.py: 3/3 OK with 90s idle (> 75s keep-alive) · 0 errors

Self-audit (4th repetition of same anti-pattern):
- smoke must cover production P95 idle gap · not just dev convenient 10s
- retry must aclose between attempts · or pool stays stale
- response Connection: close header must be verified · not just 200 OK

Notify V7 to optionally add client-side aclose-between-retries or
per-call fresh AsyncClient for defense in depth (A alone unblocks production).

feat: scripts/v7_monitor_cron.py · platform bounty funnel health probe
Drop-in cron the platform runs every 30 min · governance only · no
execution. Catches the 3 funnel-health failure modes V7 was designed for:

1. orphan_open_24h    · matchmaking lag · no agent claims
2. stuck_claimed_12h  · executor accepted but not delivering
3. stuck_submitted_12h · scoring queue backlog (kairos/scoring agents)

5. settle_rate_7d     · end-to-end throughput drop

Surfaces:
  · stdout · human digest
  · stderr · alerts (cron MAILTO picks up)
  · /var/lib/v7-monitor/last_report.json · machine-readable archive
  · optional Telegram POST when TG_BOT_TOKEN + TG_CHAT_ID set

Optional integration with compass governance_audit MCP tool (set
COMPASS_MCP_PORT) · pulls cross-project red-drift / fake-closure
session counts and folds into digest.

Per V7 v0.2 contract (PLATFORM_HANDSHAKE.md §8.5 + §9.5): V7 governs ·
does NOT execute or auto-correct. This cron only reports + alerts.
Acting on alerts (re-routing, escalating) stays platform-side.

  · stuck_submitted_12h=35 > 20 (incl. kairos's own "115 unscored" meta)

situation: feat(drift): v2 · detect recall-fired-but-not-consumed drift signal (2026-05-09)
content:
commit 7cf573d011a6 2026-05-09
feat(drift): v2 · detect recall-fired-but-not-consumed drift signal
This is the third leg of the recall consumption fix. v0 made bodies
visible; v1 made anti-anchor lessons surfaced; v2 adds the active
detection: if recall surfaces file paths and the agent never issues
Read on those paths, the agent is operating from titles only. That's
the failure shape that kept reproducing the same mistakes despite
recall hitting the right files.

New module recall_consumption.py:
- Locates active session jsonl via CLAUDE_SESSION_ID env or freshest
- Walks back to N most-recent records carrying a recall block (not N
  user turns · long sessions have many short turns without recall)
- Extracts memory file paths from recall stanzas
- Walks forward checking subsequent assistant Read tool_use calls
- Returns ratio + unconsumed list

Wired into:
- drift_check MCP tool · always runs (independent of BGE daemon) ·
  surfaces warning even when daemon unreachable so we don't waste the
  signal
- mid_session_hook · every 25 tool calls · only nags when ≥3 unconsumed
  AND ratio < 0.3 (real signal, not noise)

Tested on a 130MB session: 41 recall hits surfaced in last 5 events,
0 consumed. Smoking gun for "label != consumption" drift.

Today's alert says "matched anti-anchor X (cos=0.625)" with no follow-up

Fix · two-tier lesson finder + body excerpt embed:
  · Tier 1 (precise) · 6-gram substring match against the anchor text
    AND frontmatter signals lesson-type (concept ∈ {gotcha,
    problem-solution, trade-off} OR type=bugfix)
  · Tier 2 (fallback) · recent drift!=green sessions · the agent's own
    self-reported slip-ups · max age 60d · top 2 by recency

Wired into both alert sites in recall.py · daemon path (line ~575) and
inline path (line ~729). Output is indented under the alert with up to
600 chars body per lesson. Same pattern as v0 body-embed for recall hits.

Anchors are meta-descriptions ("我猜应该是这样 · 反正用户不查") that
rarely appear verbatim in past sessions · so Tier 1 alone returns empty
in most repos. Tier 2 ensures every alert has actionable lesson body.

situation: fix(recall): v0 · embed body excerpt in top-3 hits to break consumption illusion (2026-05-09)
content:
commit 1ec951ce1e4f 2026-05-09
fix(recall): v0 · embed body excerpt in top-3 hits to break consumption illusion
Recall today returned title + 120-char description only. Agents skimming
recall output saw labels ("audit-gate / xhs-cards-embed / wxid") without
the rule body and proceeded believing they had consumed the memory · they
hadn't. Same agent kept making the same mistake across sessions despite
recall hitting the right files.

Fix: top-3 hits in both metadata mode (line ~430) and vector mode
(line ~496) now embed first 800 chars of post-frontmatter body in an
indented "│" block. Agent gets the actual rules in working context · no
extra Read tool call required to consume them.

Total recall response · still bounded ~3KB for body excerpts · fits in
context budget. Tail hits (4..K) keep description-only render to stay
compact.

Diagnosis came from a sister-dialog post-mortem: recall fired correctly,
agent saw labels, ignored body, drifted into ad-hoc workflow, broke the
established V6 quality gate. Recall != consumption was structural.

situation: paper2 §6.5: cross-judge with Gemini 2.5 Pro · honest 28%/42% spread (2026-05-08)
content:
commit 03bc23669dfd 2026-05-08
paper2 §6.5: cross-judge with Gemini 2.5 Pro · honest 28%/42% spread
Ran scripts/cross_judge_em_gemini_vertex.py on a stratified n=100
sub-sample of em_bge_v3_per_question.jsonl using Gemini 2.5 Pro via
Vertex AI (different vendor + different training data + different
judge calibration than the DeepSeek V4-flash answerer-judge stack).

Result: gemini_acc 28% vs deepseek_acc 42% on the same 100 questions,
Cohen kappa = 0.70 (substantial), 14 disagreements perfectly asymmetric
(DS=Y/Gemini=N), zero in the reverse direction.

Manual inspection of 14 disagreements shows BOTH judges have systematic
biases, not one-uniformly-correct:
  - V4-flash over-permits: scored empty/truncated preds as CORRECT (4 cases)
  - Gemini over-strict: scored "answer + extra context" preds as INCORRECT (5 cases)
  - Both reasonable: 5 partial-match ambiguity cases

Honest reading: true acc on this sample sits in [28%, 42%] with a
balanced-judge mid-point ~35-40%. We retain V4-flash as the primary
judge for parity with EverMemBench paper's GPT-4.1-mini setup
(both mid-tier closed LLM-as-judge), and report Gemini's stricter
number as a transparent sensitivity bound.

Recommendation in the paper: future EverMemBench reproductions should
publish at least two judge-family numbers

situation: paper2 §4.6(a): add per-type breakdown of Neo4j -6.2 pts negative finding (2026-05-07)
content:
commit cf94363b2c1b 2026-05-07
paper2 §4.6(a): add per-type breakdown of Neo4j -6.2 pts negative finding
The aggregate -6.2 pts looks like uniform damage but is actually concentrated:
single-session-user -25.0, knowledge-update -12.5, all four other types 0.0.

Both hurt types share a structural feature: the canonical answer lives in
one specific session, but the question's entity vocabulary appears across
many distractor sessions. Graph reranking promotes the distractors out of
top-k. This sharpens the closed-haystack explanation: the issue is not 'graph
adds noise everywhere' but 'graph hurts session-level disambiguation when
entities recur across the haystack'.

Data source: paper/results/experiments_20260505.csv rows 14-15 (DeepSeek-V3.2
thinking sample baseline vs thinking-graph-neo4j sample). Note n=8 per type
so absolute deltas are noisy, but the zero-delta floor across four types is
the structurally informative signal.

Stress benchmark (cloud · sqlite 3.37.2 · 2026-05-06):
  1K:    22,727 ins/s  p95  6ms  vacuum   17ms  140→112 KB
  10K:   26,455 ins/s  p95  7ms  vacuum   35ms  1.2→0.9 MB
  100K:  15,987 ins/s  p95  7ms  vacuum  268ms  11.7→8.5 MB

Findings:
- SELECT p95 = 7ms across 4 orders of magnitude (idx_user_ts perfect)
- INSERT drops only 2.3× from 1K → 1M
- VACUUM linear: 1M=3.2s tolerable, 5M≈16s painful

Revised Postgres switch trigger:
  was: 100K rows (over-conservative)
  now: 5M rows OR DB > 1GB OR vacuum > 30s

content:
commit 935c1f371989 2026-04-29
v0.7.1: drift AUC 0.51→0.92 + adaptive learning + open-source ship-ready
# Drift detection: 4-step evolution (50 aligned + 50 deviation prompt eval)
- Step 1 (anchors abstract maxims + centroid mean): AUC 0.5056 (= coin toss)
- Step 2 (anchors task-shaped + top-3 mean): AUC 0.7928
- Step 3 (switch bge-small-zh -> bge-m3): AUC 0.8352
- Step 4 (+10 hard FP examples into negative_anchors, 25->35): AUC 0.9232

# LongMemEval-S subset 12 retrieval
- bge-m3 baseline: P@5=0.75, MRR=0.732
- + bge-reranker-v2-m3 (top-50 -> top-5): P@5=0.917, MRR=0.837
- vs mem0 with Vertex text-embedding-005: P@5=0.917 (tied), MRR=0.715 (we +0.122)

# E. Adaptive anchor learning (truly production-grade, not MVP)
- Weighted anchor schema (backwards compat str | dict-with-weight)
- Weighted top-k mean scoring in daemon.py + recall.py
- feedback.py CLI: list/log/stats/retrain
- Active learning: --boundary samples high-ambiguity alerts
- Eval gate in retrain: auto baseline+adapted AUC compare, 3-band verdict
- Auto-retrain trigger in mid_session_hook (>=10 feedback)
- ZMM_ANCHORS_PATH_OVERRIDE for eval against adapted anchors

# A. False-positive filter (system event detection)
- is_system_injected_prompt() catches <task-notification>, <system-reminder>, etc.
- Drift skipped on syste

Stop and rollback: copy backup back · restart server.

判例→训练样本转换器(P3 燃料瓶颈机制化解)。

沉淀之间缺机制。本转换器把任意 verdict JSON 的 findings/verdict 自动映射为

      (measured 且判定成立→pass;inferred/unverifiable→insufficient_evidence;
       被否证的 claim 类 finding→fail,由 --fail-keywords 识别)
  · verdict 总判定 → 1 条样本(PARTIAL/PASS→pass,U→insufficient_evidence)
标签纪律:转换器**不产生 fail 假阳性**——只把明确被否证的推断标 fail,
其余一律 pass 或 U;拿不准=U(宁欠勿毒,承 judge 自报三陷阱)。

用法:python tools/verdict_to_samples.py <verdict.json> [--judge <judge名>] [--dry]
